title: Geometric specialization slices of the vanishing topos
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring (a local principal ideal domain of dimension one), $B=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $f:T\to B$ a finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring annihilated by an integer invertible on $B$, and $L\in D^b(T_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$. Choose a geometric closed point $\bar b$ [def-weil-geometric-point] of $B$, its strict localization $B_{(\bar b)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and a geometric generic point $\bar t\to B_{(\bar b)}$ with its specialization to $\bar b$. Put $T_{(\bar b)}=T\times_BB_{(\bar b)}$, $T_{\bar b}=T\times_B\bar b$, $T_{\bar t}=T_{(\bar b)}\times_{B_{(\bar b)}}\bar t$, and let $i:T_{\bar b}\to T_{(\bar b)}$, $j:T_{\bar t}\to T_{(\bar b)}$ be the natural maps. The specialization defines a geometric morphism $e_f:(T_{\bar b})_{\mathrm{Et}}\to V_f$, where $V_f$ and $R\Psi_f$ are as in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$e_f^*R\Psi_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*Rj_*(L|_{T_{\bar t}}).$$
For any $B$-morphism $h:T'\to T$, with induced $v:V_{f'}\to V_f$ and $h_{\bar b}:T'_{\bar b}\to T_{\bar b}$, this isomorphism identifies the pullback of the ordinary comparison $v^*R\Psi_fL\to R\Psi_{f'}h^*L$ with the ordinary comparison for $i^*Rj_*$ induced by $h$. It also identifies the restriction of the lax tensor map of $R\Psi_f$ with the lax tensor map of $i^*Rj_*$, using the canonical derived tensor comparison for inverse image. Neither compatibility asserts that the individual ordinary or tensor comparison is invertible.

proof.text: Write $A=B_{(\bar b)}$. In the universal property of $V_f$, take $a:(T_{\bar b})_{\mathrm{Et}}\to T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ to be the fibre map, and $b:(T_{\bar b})_{\mathrm{Et}}\to\mathbf{Set}\xrightarrow{\bar t}B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ to be the constant geometric generic point. The chosen specialization gives $b\Rightarrow fa$ by composing $\bar t\Rightarrow\bar b$ with the structure morphism to $\mathbf{Set}$. Thus the universal property gives $e_f$, with $p_1e_f=a$, $p_2e_f=b$ and the specified $2$-cell. In particular it uses the generic point as its second leg, rather than the special point.

Construct the sliced comparison $\alpha_L:e_f^*R\psi_{f,*}L\to i^*Rj_*(L|_{T_{\bar t}})$ by restriction on the triple site, as in (1.3.4). More explicitly, the inverse image of $(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ under $\psi_f$ is $U\times_VW$. Pointed compatible lifts to $\bar b$ and $\bar t$ restrict this object to the generic fibre over $A$. The restriction maps of a direct-image resolution therefore give the comparison on the inverse-image presheaf; their compatibility with refinement makes it a map after sheafification and derivation. Use the same restriction maps for all inputs, so $\alpha$ is a natural transformation, before taking stalks. At a geometric $x$ of $T_{\bar b}$ its map is the restriction from the triple-neighbourhood limit (the Milnor tube) to $T_{(x)}\times_A\bar t$. The oriented-point cohomology lemma identifies its source with that tube's derived sections. No base-change isomorphism for arbitrary squares is being assumed here.

source.place: section 1.3, construction and equality in (1.3.4); section 1.4 for the comparison convention

proof.text: For a geometric point $x$ of $T_{\bar b}$, let $x_A$ and $x_T$ be its images in $T_A$ and $T$. The strict-base closed-point localization lemma gives $(T_A)_{(x_A)}\cong T_{(x_T)}$, compatibly with $A$. On the classical side, compute a stalk of $Rj_*$ on pointed affine etale neighbourhoods $U$ of $x_A$: in degree $n$ it is $\varinjlim_U H^n(U\times_A\bar t,L)$. The higher-direct-image presheaf formula supplies this description for a sheaf, and the bounded-below truncation spectral sequence supplies it for $L$. The schemes $U\times_A\bar t$ are affine with affine transition maps, so derived etale continuity identifies this colimit with $H^n(T_{(x_T)}\times_A\bar t,L)$. Forgetting constant coefficients computes the same cohomology; the forgetful comparison extends from sheaves to $L$ by that spectral sequence. Hence the stalk of $\alpha_L$ is exactly restriction from the Milnor tube to this geometric generic fibre.

Let $k^s$ be the separable algebraic closure of the generic residue field of $B$ in $\kappa(\bar t)$; the strict localization at that generic point is $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$. The tube in the preceding step is the affine $k^s$-scheme $M=T_{(x_T)}\times_A\operatorname{Spec}k^s$. Put $\bar k$ equal to the algebraic closure of $k^s$ inside $\kappa(\bar t)$. Then $\bar k/k^s$ is purely inseparable, so its spectrum is integral, radicial and surjective and hence a universal homeomorphism. Topological invariance identifies cohomology of $M$ and $M_{\bar k}$. Apply the field-extension higher-image exchange lemma to the affine scheme $M_{\bar k}$ and the extension $\kappa(\bar t)/\bar k$: every cohomology sheaf is killed by the given invertible integer. It gives the same cohomology after this extension, and the truncation spectral sequence gives the assertion for bounded $L$. Thus every cohomology stalk of $\alpha_L$ is invertible, so derived-stalk conservativity proves $\alpha_L$ is the asserted isomorphism. This also handles geometric points whose fields are not algebraic over their images.

source.place: section 1.3, (1.3.2)--(1.3.4); field enlargement justified by Stacks 0F1C and topological invariance

proof.text: For $h:T'\to T$ over $B$, the universal property gives $v e_{f'}=e_f h_{\bar b}$. The claimed square therefore has top map $h_{\bar b}^*e_f^*R\Psi_fL\to e_{f'}^*R\Psi_{f'}h^*L$, not a map obtained by pulling along $e_f$ alone. Its bottom map is $h_{\bar b}^*i^*Rj_*L_{\bar t}\to i'^*Rj'_*h_{\bar t}^*L_{\bar t}$. Expand each ordinary comparison as its mate: first the unit for the primed direct image, then the inverse-image square, then pullback of the unprimed counit. In the triple-site models defining $\alpha$, these are respectively insertion of the adjunction unit, pullback of a section along $h$, and evaluation of that section. Restriction to the geometric generic fibre commutes with all three operations: both composites send a section to its pullback along $h$ and then its restriction. Thus the square commutes already for the resolution comparisons and hence in the derived categories. The argument applies to arbitrary $h$, even if $f'$ is not finite type.

source.place: section 1.4, (1.4.1)--(1.4.3), together with the restriction construction (1.3.4)

proof.text: Use the derived tensor-pullback isomorphism for arbitrary ringed topoi, with constant coefficient rings, for $e_f$ and $\psi_f$ as well as for $i$ and $j$. Resolve tensor inputs by K-flat complexes. The lax map for a direct image is the mate of the tensor of its two counits. In the restriction models of step 2, the counit evaluates a section, and the tensor of counits sends $a\otimes b$ to the tensor of their evaluations. Restricting this tensor to the generic fibre gives $\operatorname{res}(a)\otimes\operatorname{res}(b)$, exactly the result of restricting the two sections first and then taking the tensor of the $j$-counits. The tensor-pullback isomorphism identifies these targets. The bijection defining mates therefore gives the desired commutative tensor-comparison square. This is an equality of natural derived maps from the resolution construction, not an inference of equality from equality on cohomology stalks. The ordinary and lax tensor comparisons themselves need not be invertible.

source.place: counit construction of the lax tensor map; Stacks 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; not a claim of section 1.4
